added.summary: `::slotted(<compound>)` in a component's sheet selects the top-level elements of the content rendered at its `{@render}` sites, from the element around the site: `.body::slotted(p) { margin: 0 }`, or bare `::slotted(p)` for every site. The rule ranks under the rules of the document that wrote the content, as CSS ranks a shadow tree's rules on slotted content, and `!important` reverses that. A component instance passed as content is selected by its root's tag, classes and attributes, and there the rule wins over the component's own rules for its root. Before, `::slotted()` was refused.

`:has-slotted` matches the element around a `{@render}` site while content passed to the component (elements or component instances) is rendered there, and not for the component's own fallback snippet: `.footer:has-slotted { padding: 8px }`. Before, it was refused.
